full_judgment:
The petitioners, joint Mutawallis of Saber Khan Wakf Estate filed O.C. Suit No.5 of 1969 in the Court of subordinate Judge, Noakhali for declaration that the suit properties of the Wakf Estate were not affected by Ordinance III of 1956 and by the Special Notification of 1954 and prayed for restraining the respondents from interfering with the management and collection of rents by them till proper annuity is fixed and compensation is assessed for the tenanted and khas lands of the Wakf Estate. 

 The Courts below found that the Compensation Assessment Rolls were finally published on 1.3.57 and 10.11.61 in the Official Gazette and accordingly the interest of the proprietors vested in the Provincial Government pursuant to Section 44 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Mr. Khan found it difficult to press this point further. He then contended that the petitioners filed rent cases which are pending and these are evidences of the act of possession by them, but the High Court Division failed to consider this aspect of the case. The question of petitioners being in possession is of no consequence, because of the fact that the Compensation Assessment rolls have already been published and the right of the mutawallis to continue in possession came to and ends under the provision of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. We, therefore, find no substance in the contention of the learned Counsel.
